originalTitle: Global Market: Geopolitical risks return to centre stage for ECB as inflation fears resurface
simplifiedContent: There's been an increase in tensions between the US and Iran, which is affecting the European Central Bank's (ECB) plans. The ECB was focusing on controlling inflation, but now energy prices are rising again, which could lead to higher prices across Europe. This uncertainty is making it harder for the ECB to make decisions about interest rates. As a result, investors think the ECB will raise interest rates again, which could impact the economy. This means that what happens in the Middle East will play a big role in deciding the ECB's future monetary policy.

originalTitle: Newgen Software shares surge 15% as broad-based IT stocks rally
simplifiedContent: Newgen Software's stock price jumped 15% because other IT companies' stocks were also doing well. The company recently made some important changes, including choosing a new CEO named Tarun Nandwani. Investors are waiting to see how the company did financially in the first quarter of the year, which will be announced on July 16. This will give them an idea of how the business is doing and what to expect in the future. The stock's recent movement suggests it might be gaining strength, which could be interesting for investors to watch.

originalTitle: Why TCS employee addition just hit 4-year high amid AI job loss fears
simplifiedContent: TCS, a big IT company, just hired 9,279 new employees, which is the most they've hired in a quarter in four years. This is surprising because many people are worried that artificial intelligence (AI) will replace human workers and lead to job losses. However, TCS thinks that AI will actually change the types of jobs people do, rather than get rid of them altogether. The company is investing in new technologies and hiring more people, which suggests they're feeling positive about their future growth. This matter because it shows that TCS is confident in its ability to adapt to changes in the industry and keep growing.

originalTitle: Gillette India reschedules board meeting date to declare dividend. Record date, other details
simplifiedContent: Gillette India, a company listed on the stock market, has changed the date of its board meeting. At this meeting, the company will decide how much dividend (a portion of its profits) to give to its shareholders. The original announcement didn't mention the new date, but it will be important for investors to know when it is. This matters because the dividend payment can affect the company's stock price and the amount of money shareholders receive. By changing the meeting date, the company is adjusting its timeline for making this important decision.

originalTitle: Small-cap industrial stock Interarch Building Products extends gains after this business update; details here
simplifiedContent: A company called Interarch Building Products, which is a small company that makes industrial products, recently shared some business news. They announced that they have opened a new factory in a place called Kheda, Gujarat, in India. This means the company is expanding and can now make more products, which could be good for its business. As a result, the company's stock price has gone up, which is a positive sign for investors who own the stock. This update is important because it shows that the company is growing and increasing its presence in India.

originalTitle: Natural gas companies are set to lose steam in Q1
simplifiedContent: Some companies that deal with natural gas, like GAIL and Petronet LNG, are expected to have weaker financial results for the first quarter of their fiscal year. This is because they are importing less natural gas, paying more to get the gas they need, and facing problems getting gas due to a war in West Asia. These issues will likely affect how much money these companies make. As a result, their earnings for the first quarter may not be as good as expected, which could be important for investors to know. This might impact the companies' performance and potentially affect their stock prices.
